r0144_conclusion.classification: The seeded row is none of "impossible" and none of "permitted audit representation of conformant data": it is DEFECTIVE persisted data. The locked snapshot rule already resolves its meaning (non-conformant); no owner decision is needed.
r0144_conclusion.producible_by_the_pipeline: No. EligibilityDecisionService returns a reason on every eligible=0 branch and EodEligibilityBuildService leads the set with the suspension reason; every code the two producers can emit is a registered active code (B19EligibilityReasonRegistrationTest, against the reason-code registry seed). The real run has one blocked row with a one-member registered set.
r0144_conclusion.was_it_prevented_after_production: No - this was the gap. replaceEligibility() required the fact fields to be non-blank and "[]" is non-blank; no schema constraint and no seal/admission step checked it (the semantic hash covers the set but does not judge it). So a blocked row with an empty set could be persisted by a producer defect or a bypass, and the export, which reports what was stored, could not make R0144 true for it.
r0144_conclusion.what_the_export_may_do: Report the persisted row as stored. It must not invent a reason (reviewer and fail-safe rule) and refusing to describe a publication would hide the defect from the audit artifact. The seeded row is therefore still exported as stored - but the test and basis now say it is non-conformant data reported faithfully, not a conformant blocked row.
r0144_conclusion.correction: F-MD-B19-A001-009 (P3, RESOLVED): replaceEligibility() refuses, before deleting or inserting anything, an eligible=0 row whose eligibility_reasons_json is not a non-empty JSON list of non-blank strings (ELIGIBILITY_WRITE_INCOMPLETE). Snapshot and promote copies are not tightened (they must not reject legacy history). Registry membership is not enforced in the write path (proven for the producer literals and the real run).
r0144_conclusion.proof_gap_closed: R0144 previously rested on the producer and one real blocked row; the exceptional case the contract also governs (a blocked row without a usable set) had no guard. It now has one at the only write entry for new eligibility rows.

r0134_conclusion: A NULL listing_id in a sealed publication is possible only for a legacy (V1) row: the column is nullable and the write path does not require it, but a V2 semantic artifact cannot be formed from it - the identity key the semantic hash navigates by refuses NULL, 0 or absent listing ids (ARTIFACT_LOCAL_NAVIGATION_KEY_MISSING), proven by execution. The export reports a legacy NULL as NULL and never substitutes the ticker or the publication id (E02, E03). No production change and no owner decision.
r0138_conclusion: A NULL reason set cannot be written (REQUIRED_ELIGIBILITY_WRITE_FIELDS; the existing StageThreeWriteCompletenessGuardTest data set and B19EligibilityBlockedRowAdmissionTest) so an unrecorded set is legacy-only and is exported as an empty cell, never rebuilt. An invalid representation (not a list, blank or non-string member) on a blocked row is now refused at the write. For a usable row an unusual set is mirrored as stored. The cell encoding remains the persisted JSON array verbatim (scope note of E-011, unchanged).
